source_span: With the 10-year above 5%, bearish duration positioning close to historical extremes and inflation and credibility premia increasingly embedded in long-end yields, 25bp of tightening at the front end may now be the most bond-friendly outcome available to the Fed.
source_chain: 10-year at 5%+ with DB bond positioning at the 5th percentile (near-record bearish, 'almost nobody left to sell') therefore a hike that would normally sell off bonds instead reads as a credibility move that caps the inflation/term premium the market had been pricing in therefore the hike itself becomes the bond-friendly outcome and yields can rally on the news; invalidation/uncertainty: this is tactical not structural — CTA convexity means a reversal lower in yields forces momentum shorts to cover (amplifying any rally), but DB's own history shows yields typically keep rising ~114bp in the year after a first hike, so whether the rally holds depends on the market's read of the decision rather than the hike itself.
pulse_chain: Fed delivers the most hawkish hike on the table (25bp to 3.75-4.00%, 16 of 18 officials seeing another hike, long-run dot to 3.25%, cross-checked against Goldman's own recap) therefore, given bond positioning already at DB's 5th-percentile bearish extreme with 'almost nobody left to do the selling,' the hawkish outcome removes the fear of the Fed falling behind rather than confirming it therefore the 10-year rallies back to 4.95% instead of extending Tuesday's selloff, and the pulse's own prior short-$TLT call (built on sub-5% yields) paid when 5% broke; forward condition: whether the priced 51% odds of an October hike land decides if this is CTA/momentum shorts closing out (per the note's own convexity point) or a genuine trend turn, with Goldman (Oct) and JPMorgan (Dec) disagreeing on timing but agreeing on the terminal rate.
why: The pulse keeps the note's exact mechanism (extreme bearish positioning turns a hawkish, normally bond-bearish hike into a relief rally) and its own hedge about whether the move is forced short-covering versus a real turn, in different words and compressed with facts drawn from the day's actual FOMC outcome rather than the pre-meeting preview.
